en: Touching an exposed wire with wet hands is dangerous because water lowers your skin's electrical resistance, increasing shock risk.
Applying sunscreen blocks harmful ultraviolet light energy from the sun, preventing skin damage and reducing skin cancer risk.
Using a wheelbarrow, a second-class lever, allows you to lift heavy soil with less effort, protecting your back from strain.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes with deep treads increases friction on wet floors, preventing slips and falls during the rainy season.
Swallowing small neodymium magnets is extremely dangerous because they attract each other inside your intestines, causing severe tissue damage.
Listening to loud music through earphones for over an hour can permanently damage the tiny hair cells in your inner ear.
Staring directly at a laser pointer can permanently burn your retina because it concentrates intense light energy into a tiny spot.
Wearing a hard hat protects your head from the kinetic energy of falling objects accelerated by Earth's constant gravitational pull.
Eating a banana provides your body with chemical energy, which your cells convert into kinetic energy to run and play.
Plugging too many appliances into one extension cord causes overheating because excess electrical current generates dangerous thermal energy in wires.
Pushing a heavy box up a ramp, an inclined plane, requires less force than lifting it, preventing muscle injuries.
Using a wooden spoon instead of a metal one to stir hot soup prevents thermal energy from conducting quickly and burning your hand.
